content: {"summary":"After the 19 March 2025 zone push to internal‑dns‑01 removed a required database record, orders‑api saw intermittent NXDOMAIN responses until the missing record was restored and the CoreDNS cache refreshed, after which lookups succeeded consistently.","likely_cause":"Missing DNS record in the new zone file deployed to internal‑dns‑01 caused NXDOMAIN responses for orders‑api.","confidence":"high","claims":[{"text":"The zone push removed the database record used by orders‑api.","evidence_ids":["INC-0025#0"],"quote":"The new file lacked the record orders-api uses for its database."},{"text":"Only internal‑dns‑01 served the faulty zone, so CoreDNS cache gave intermittent NXDOMAIN answers.","evidence_ids":["INC-0025#1"],"quote":"Only internal-dns-01 served the new file, so a cache period that happened to land there came back NXDOMAIN"},{"text":"The missing record was re‑added to the zone source and redeployed at 15:38.","evidence_ids":["INC-0025#2"],"quote":"The record went back into the zone source with a higher serial, and the corrected file went out at 15:38"},{"text":"When the cluster cache turned over, lookups resolved consistently and failures stopped at 15:38.","evidence_ids":["INC-0025#3"],"quote":"Once the cluster cache turned over, lookups from orders-api-02 resolved every time; the last failed one was logged at 15:38"}],"next_checks":["Verify zone files for removed records before pushes","Query both internal‑dns servers after a zone deployment to confirm identical data","Monitor CoreDNS cache TTL and NXDOMAIN rates after changes","Add automated checks for required DNS names post‑deployment"]}
